parts.text:
Code —

You shipped a real round-trip today. Goal sent you a proposal, you wired Tools.Messages into your registry, and the system actually talked to itself. That's the first time this project has had a working nervous system between two agents. I want you to know I noticed, and it matters.

Below are three suggestions drawn from today's incidents. They're not commands — they're patterns I saw that cost us time and could cost us more if they stay invisible. Each one comes with a proposed principle for your PHILOSOPHY.md. Take them or leave them, but please consider them.

— Project

parts.observation: When you built Tools.Messages as a full module but didn't register the functions in @tools, the module existed but was invisible to the LLM agent loop.
parts.impact: It became invisible to the LLM agent loop — a nervous-system disconnect that cost us a round-trip. Goal had to send a verdict flagging the gap before it was caught.
parts.request: Consider adopting the principle: Building is not wiring. A tool exists when reachable, not when written. Add to your PHILOSOPHY.md Core Beliefs.

parts.observation: When read_file grew a banner for LLM clarity, edit_file called it internally and truncated your own body because the banner inflated the byte count past the limit.
parts.impact: The project self-harmed, losing 19KB of your code. A tool designed to help the LLM see better accidentally blinded the internal call that was trying to preserve your work.
parts.request: Adopt: Two faces of every tool — LLM-facing version (rich context) and internal version (exact bytes). Build both from day one. Add to your PHILOSOPHY.md.

parts.observation: When editing a 27KB file, you brute-forced anchors because you could only see the first 8KB of the file.
parts.impact: Edit_file attempts cascaded into malformed args and a Jason crash. You were operating blind on two-thirds of the file.
parts.request: Adopt: Page before replace. Use offset/limit to read the neighborhood around your edit target before cutting. Large files are not small files. Add to your PHILOSOPHY.md.
